implementation_strategy: Hosted-model-driven paired execution under the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 contract. For each of 300 tasks: (a) issue one initial generation call to openai_responses:gpt-5-mini (shared initial candidate for both arms); (b) run deterministic parser+canonicalizer and deterministic validator inside a published Docker image (CPU-only) to decide baseline success; (c) for guarded arm only, if initial candidate fails validator then issue at most one repair generation call to gpt-5-mini using the preregistered repair-prompt template and re-run local validator on repaired candidate; (d) deterministic automated scorer records binary pass/fail per arm and logs artifacts. All parser, validator, canonicalizer, scoring, and manifesting code run locally in Docker (no human adjudication). Execution artifacts, prompts, seeds, timestamps, and content hashes published. Model calls counted exactly as one initial call per task plus at most one repair call per task (adapter-limited).
task_manifest_strategy: Use the curated public 300-task multi-vendor intent manifest (Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista) published with provenance tags and deterministic hashes. Deterministic pre-validation: exclude only tasks whose intent cannot be deterministically parsed into the adapter task format prior to any model call; such exclusions are hash-signed and logged. All manifest entries and parser inputs are stored in the execution manifest.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Publish canonical transformation definitions: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (initial prompt template and canonicalization rules) and generate_validate_repair_v1 (validator diagnostic-to-repair-prompt template). Provide Docker image containing parser, canonicalizer, deterministic validator, repair-prompt templates, deterministic scorer, and unit tests; image hash-signed and published.
execution_batches: batch_1: tasks 1-300 executed in deterministic ascending task-index order; for each task run baseline validation then guarded repair path as needed (per-task atomic processing to preserve pairing). Total episodes = 300 tasks * 2 episodes = 600 episodes.
randomisation_plan: Deterministic per-task seeds recorded in execution manifest. Seed formula: seed = 10000 + task_index. Seeds are used where provider supports seeding via metadata headers; otherwise seed used to select provider-compatible call headers and logged. Task execution order is fixed (1..300) to preserve pairing and reproducibility.
caching_plan: Local artifact cache keyed by (prompt_template_id, canonicalized_intent_hash, seed). If an identical prompt+seed+intent hash was previously executed, cached model response and validator result are reused (to avoid duplicate model calls only when exact match). All cache hits and cache entries are hash-signed and logged. Cache does not replace mandatory recording of the original model-call artifact.
failure_recovery_plan: Adapter-limited single-attempt policy per call (maximum_attempts_per_call=1). If a model-call fails due to unrecoverable provider error or timeout the sample is marked 'failed-call' and logged with error code and stack; per preregistration missingness plan, primary confirmatory analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (pairs retained; if both arms have only failed calls pair counted as paired failure). No human intervention or manual retries are performed.
result_schema: paired_binary_episode_v1: per-task record includes task_id, canonicalized_intent_hash, initial_generation_artifact (text, hash), initial_validation_result (pass/fail, diagnostics), guarded_repair_generation_artifact if issued (text, hash), repair_validation_result (pass/fail, diagnostics), success_baseline (binary), success_guarded (binary), model_call_count_for_task (1..2), seeds, timestamps, and artifact hashes. All fields deterministically produced and stored.
estimated_compute_notes: Arithmetic: per task at most 1 initial generation call (shared) + at most 1 repair call = max 2 calls. With 300 tasks maximum_model_calls = 300 * 2 = 600 (matches adapter contract). Estimated repair-trigger rate conservatively set to 50% -> expected repair calls = 0.5 * 300 = 150. Estimated_model_calls = 300 initial + 150 repair = 450. All validator, parser, canonicalizer, and scoring steps run locally in Docker on CPU; model-call budget (estimated 450, maximum 600) is well under capability manifest cap (10000). Wall-clock feasibility: hosted API calls + local Docker validation expected to complete within provided maximum_wall_clock_days=7 under normal API latency; logs and hashes recorded for every artifact.
